key_insight: You can align an LLM for safety in a single (high-resource) language and enforce multilingual consistency so the safety behavior transfers to many other languages without heavy per-language supervision.
problem_solved: Scalable multilingual safety alignment: current methods require large target-language datasets or costly pairwise alignment, which limits deployment across many languages.
method: Perform safety alignment once in a source language using existing supervised/alignment procedures.
Create multilingual views (via translation or parallel data) and add a consistency/agreement objective that enforces the aligned safety behavior across languages.
Leverage synthetic translations and consistency regularization to avoid large-scale, high-quality annotations or exhaustive pairwise alignment.
impact: Makes multilingual safety practical and cost-efficient: practitioners can extend aligned LLM behavior to many languages with far less annotation and engineering overhead, improving global safe deployment.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: 'Align once' (single-language) → consistency module → multiple target languages (many arrows)
Agreement/consistency icon: parallel inputs (same prompt in different languages) mapped to the same safe response with a loss/regularizer symbol
Bar chart comparing resource cost: per-language supervised alignment vs. single-source + consistency approach
World map with language icons showing widespread deployment from one alignment step
paper_title: Align Once, Benefit Multilingually: Enforcing Multilingual Consistency for LLM Safety Alignment
paper_authors: Yuyan Bu, Xiaohao Liu, ZhaoXing Ren, Yaodong Yang, Juntao Dai
